### Wandering Far and Near

The itinerary began modestly enough: a few nights at a [hostel]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hostel · n. 旅社，招待所"} outside [Madrid]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Madrid · n. 马德里"}, then a slow train east toward the [Venice]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Venice · n. 威尼斯"} of the north. The second leg took us farther: a [safari]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="safari · n. 旅行；狩猎远征；旅行队"} camp in the [tropic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tropic · n. 回归线; 热带, 热带地方"}s, where the [gutter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="gutter · n. 排水沟；槽；贫民区; 流；形成沟; 开沟于…；弄熄; 贫贱的；粗俗的；耸人听闻的"} of a night rainstorm ran in silver threads off the reed roof; a [ghetto]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ghetto · n. 犹太人区；贫民区; 使集中居住"} neighborhood in a port city that had quietly become its most painterly [venue]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="venues · n. 犯罪现场，发生地点；场地，场馆"} for street art; a river settlement beside the [Tigris]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Tigris · n. 底格里斯河"} that reminded us, impossibly, of illustrations from a book on ancient [Persia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Persia · n. 波斯"}. ### Wanderers, Walls, and Windows

The [voyage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="voyage · n. 航行；航程；旅行记; 航海；航行; 飞过；渡过"} began at dawn, when the last stars were still fading above the [hilltop]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="hilltop · n. 小山顶"} monastery. We had studied maps of [Eurasia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Eurasia · n. 欧亚大陆"} for months — from the ancient streets of [Ephesus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Ephesus · n. 以弗所"} to the river bends of [Babylon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Babylon · n. 巴比伦,奢华淫靡的城市,任何大的富庶的或罪恶的城市"} — yet nothing prepares you for the moment a [far-off]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="far-off · adj. 遥远的"} skyline finally resolves into stone and smoke.

Our first stop was a [cottage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cottage · n. 村舍；小屋；小别墅"} tucked inside a walled [enclave]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="enclave · n. 飞地；被包围的领土；被包围物"} at the edge of the old city. A narrow [archway]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="archway · n. 拱门,拱道"} led us in, its keystone worn smooth by centuries of passing hands. Above the [doorway]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="doorway · n. 门口；途径"}, someone had painted a small sun. Inside, the [ceiling]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="ceiling · n. 天花板，顶棚; 最高限度，上限; 高度，上升限度；云幕高度"} was low and vaulted, and a crooked [chimney]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="chimney · n. 烟囱, 烟筒"} rose from the kitchen hearth like a punctuation mark against the morning sky. We shared a [cubicle]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="cubicle · n. 小卧室, 斗室"}-sized room on the upper floor, where a [balcony]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="balcony · n. 阳台；包厢；戏院楼厅"} jutted out over a lane of herb sellers and pigeon coops.

By afternoon we had crossed into a rougher district — former [barrack]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="barrack · n. 营房,兵营; 棚屋,工房; 外观简陋划一的房屋; 向...提供营房; 使住入营房; 大叫, 喝倒彩起…"} buildings repurposed into studios, each one occupying a modest [acreage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="acreage · n. 英亩数; 土地面积;"} of courtyard — and stood before the grandest [edifice]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="edifice · n. 大建筑物"} on the square: a civic hall whose [African]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="African · adj. 非洲的，非洲人的; 非洲人"} granite columns had been shipped, so the plaque read, from a quarry near [Baghdad]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Baghdad · n. 巴格达"}. The architect had been born in [Cologne]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Cologne 科隆"}, trained in [Belgium]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Belgium · n. 比利时"}, and had spent a restless decade moving between [Georgia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Georgia · n. 美国佐治亚州; 格鲁吉亚; 乔治娅"}, [Bolivia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Bolivia · n. 玻利维亚"}, [Ecuador]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Ecuador · n. 厄瓜多尔"}, [Jamaica]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Jamaica · n. 牙买加,牙买加甜酒"}, [Croatia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Croatia · n. 克罗地亚"}, and [Belarus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Belarus 白俄罗斯"} before settling here. On the steps, a guide gestured toward [yonder]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="yonder · adj. 那边的，远处的; 在那边；在远处; 那边"} ridge where [Lebanon]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Lebanon · n. 黎巴嫩"} cedars lined the old Crusader wall, and pointed out that the street below had once been the main road into the district of [Bethany]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Bethany 贝瑟尼"}.

### Traces of Civilization, Echoes of Place

Long before continents drifted apart from the primordial [pangaea]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pangaea · n. 盘古大陆；泛大陆"}, human beings were already drawn to water. The ancient [Athenian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Athenian · n. 雅典人; 雅典的；雅典人的；雅典文化的"} philosopher from [Miletus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Miletus · n. 米利都"} understood this: settle near a shore, and trade will follow. That instinct has never faded. Travelers today still trace those old routes — crossing the [Adriatic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Adriatic · adj. 亚得里亚海的；亚得里亚海沿岸居民的"}, skimming the [Atlantic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Atlantic · adj. 在大西洋里的；近大西洋的; 大西洋"}, gliding down the [Yangtze]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Yangtze · n. 长江，扬子江"}, threading through the locks of [Ontario]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Ontario · n. 安大略湖"} — as if re-stitching the seams of the world.

On land, the architecture tells the same story of arrival and shelter. In a cobbled quarter of [Tribeca]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Tribeca · n. 特里贝克地区"}, a converted [mansion]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mansion · n. 宅第，公馆；大厦"} rises behind a wrought-iron gate, its upper [terrace]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="terrace · n. 梯田；阳台；平台; 使成梯田，使成阶地；使有平台屋顶; 成阶地；成梯田；筑成坛; 叠层式的"} overlooking a [corridor]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="corridor · n. 走廊"} of narrow streets below. A [passage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="passage · n. 通路；走廊；一段"} cuts through the building's base, dark and cool, leading to a courtyard where the old [taverns]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="taverns · n. 旅馆；酒馆"} once filled with sailors off the docks. Deeper beneath the city, [tunnels]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="tunnels · n. 隧道；地下道；洞群; 凿隧道；建筑隧道"} carry thousands of commuters past foundations that predate the [suburbs]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="suburbs · n. 郊外"} by centuries. Step into an [elevator]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="elevator · n. 电梯；升降舵；升降机；起卸机"}, rise twelve floors, and the [pathway]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pathway · n. 路,径"} from street to sky takes less than a minute — yet every surface you touch was once raw earth.

The same layering appears wherever you travel. In [Calcutta]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Calcutta · n. 加尔各答,印度东北部的港市"}, in [Myanmar]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Myanmar 缅甸"}, on the [Yucatan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Yucatan 尤卡坦半岛"} coast, along the shores of [Tunisia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Tunisia · n. 突尼斯"} and [Liberia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Liberia · n. 利比里亚"}, across the plains of [Uruguay]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Uruguay · n. 乌拉圭"} and the forested hills of [Vermont]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Vermont · n. 佛蒙特州"} and [Arkansas]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Arkansas · n. 阿肯色州"}, in the university towns of [Berkeley]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Berkeley 伯克利"} and the corporate towers of the [Emirates]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Emirates · n. 阿联酋航空公司"} — buildings absorb the climate and the culture that raised them. A simple [shelter]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="shelter · n. 避难所；遮盖物；庇护; 使掩蔽；保护; 躲避，避难"} in [Oceania]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Oceania · n. 大洋洲"} and a glass tower in [Delaware]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Delaware · n. 特拉华州"} are, at root, the same impulse: stake a place, keep the elements out, make room for living.

### Wandering from the Baltic to the Tropics

The journey began in **Tallinn**, where everything felt unmistakably [Estonian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Estonian · adj. 爱沙尼亚的; 爱沙尼亚人,爱沙尼亚语"} — amber-lit cobblestones, medieval spires, and a courtyard [pavilion]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="pavilion · n. 大帐篷；阁；亭子；展示馆; 搭帐篷；置…于亭中；笼罩"} that had somehow survived every [Prussian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Prussian · adj. 普鲁士的; 普鲁士人"} incursion and [Flanders]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Flanders · n. 佛兰德斯"}-style trade war the centuries could throw at it. Standing at the [junction]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="junction · n. 连接，接合；交叉点；接合点"} of the old town and the harbour, I traced the city's [interior]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="interior · n. 内部; 内地; 内部的; 内地的, 国内的"} lanes by the glow of each [lamppost]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lamppost · n. 街灯柱；路灯柱"}, their halos dissolving into the fog rolling off the [maritime]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="maritime · adj. 海的; 航海的"} Baltic. A sleek [monorail]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="monorail · n. 单轨; 单轨索道"} ran silently overhead, threading between copper rooftops — an incongruous modernism in a city that felt frozen in amber.

From there the itinerary leapt across [landmass]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="landmass · n. 大陆"}es with the logic only long-haul flights possess. [Montreal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Montreal · n. 蒙特利尔"} in autumn, where the [Northern]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Northern · adj. 北方的；北部的; 北部方言 northernadj. 北方的, 北部的"} light turns every stone building sepia by four o'clock. A detour through [Portland]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Portland · n. 波特兰"} and on to [Oklahoma]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Oklahoma · n. 美国俄克拉荷马州"} and [Nebraska]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Nebraska · n. 内布拉斯加州"}, state signs blurring across flat [plateaus]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="plateaus · n. 高原；台地；停滞时期"} that seemed to go on longer than Paraguay itself — though [Paraguay]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Paraguay · n. 巴拉圭,巴拉圭茶"}, too, appeared later on the map, wedged between rivers I had to look up. Somewhere in a [Pasadena]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Pasadena · n. 帕萨迪纳市 ）"} side street I found a small [monument]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="monument · n. 纪念碑；历史遗迹；不朽的作品; 为…树碑"} to the city's citrus-boom past, the kind of [premises]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="premises · n. 房屋或其他建筑物; 前言，契据的缘起部分; 提出…为前提；预述"} that doubles as a heritage site and a gift shop. In [Portugal]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Portugal · n. 葡萄牙"} the same impulse manifests as [obelisks]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="obelisks · n. 方尖碑"} placed at the centre of every provincial square, pointing at a sky equally indifferent to glory and to rain.

The second half of the trip belonged to heat. In **Lebanon** — or rather in the [Lebanese]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Lebanese · adj. 黎巴嫩的; 黎巴嫩人"} hill towns above Beirut — the roads narrowed to threads along the ridgeline, and the [panorama]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="panorama · n. 全景，全貌；全景画；概论"} at dusk stretched all the way to Cyprus. Flying south over the horn of Africa, we passed above [Ethiopia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Ethiopia · n. 埃塞俄比亚"} and banked toward [Ndjamena]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Ndjamena · n. 恩贾梅纳"}, **Chad**'s capital, before continuing to the coast. The [Maldives]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Maldives · n. 马尔代夫"} leg was pure contrast: every structure raised on sand and coral, no [lavatory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="lavatory · n. 厕所，盥洗室"} more than a few metres from the sea, the entire [maritime]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="maritime · adj. 海的; 航海的"} logic of the islands expressed in the way buildings turned their backs to the noon sun and opened toward the lagoon. I thought of the [Manitoba]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Manitoba · n. 马尼托巴湖"} lakes I'd seen months before — cold, grey, enormous — and of [Pakistan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Pakistan · n. 巴基斯坦"}'s mountain roads, where hairpin bends unfolded into fresh [panorama]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="panorama · n. 全景，全貌；全景画；概论"}s every hundred metres. Geography, I decided, is just the slow [interior]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="interior · n. 内部; 内地; 内部的; 内地的, 国内的"} monologue of the planet, and travel is the only way to listen.

### A Long Day on the Road

The [itinerary]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="itinerary · n. 旅程;行程"} had looked manageable on paper: a morning [excursion]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="excursion · n. 远足, 短途旅行"} to the hilltop ruins, an afternoon drift along the broad [boulevard]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="boulevard · n. 林荫大道; 要道，大街"} that ribboned through the old quarter, and a quick stop at the [gymnasium]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="gymnasium · n. 健身房, 体育馆"} converted into a youth hostel near the [dormitory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="dormitory · n. 集体宿舍"} district. But travel, as always, rewrote the plan.

We reached the site at midday. The ruins sat at a commanding [elevation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="elevation · n. 提升, 提高, 晋级; 海拔; 正视图, 立体图"}, their broken [colonnade]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="colonnade · n. 石柱廊"} casting sharp shadows across a sun-bleached [courtyard]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="courtyard · n. 庭院, 院子"}. In the [vicinity]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="vicinity · n. 近, 接近, 密切; 附近, 邻近"}, a row of [terraced]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="terraced · adj. 台地的，阶地的；有平台的，有露台的"} houses clung to the slope like a sentence written sideways. A rusted [downspout]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="downspout · n. 〈美〉水落管"} rattled against one wall. Further down the path lay a small [graveyard]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="graveyard · n. 墓地，坟场; 垃圾场；废物堆积处；收容所"}, its stones worn smooth, and below that, half-hidden by overgrowth, the entrance to the [catacombs]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="catacombs · n. 地下墓穴,陵寝"} — narrow, cool, and oddly peaceful. Before we descended, someone found the [restroom]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="restroom · n. 公用厕所;盥洗室;卫生间"} tucked behind the ticket booth, a mercy after four hours in the sun.

By evening we were far from plan. A mechanical delay had left the group [stranded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stranded · adj. 搁浅的；陷于困境的；有…股的; 搁浅"} at a provincial junction, one bag short and one [stowaway]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stowaway · n. 偷乘船〔飞机〕者"} cat richer — the animal had slipped aboard the van outside a market in the lowlands. We scrolled through photos: the [bleachers]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="bleachers · n. 廉价座位；露天看台"} of an abandoned stadium in [Guatemala]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Guatemala · n. 危地马拉,危地马拉人"}, a [mausoleum]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mausoleum · n. 陵墓 Mausoleum公元前四世纪波斯属地Caria 地方Mausolus 王的陵墓"} modeled on the one the word itself came from, a [houseboat]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="houseboat · n. 形如房子的船,游艇"} moored on a canal whose surface caught the last light perfectly. Tomorrow the [escalator]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="escalator · n. 自动扶梯"} in the city-center station would carry us back up to the main concourse; tonight we spread maps on the floor of a café near the [Euphrates]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Euphrates · n. 幼发拉底河"} bend and traced a slower route — through [Slovenia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Slovenia · n. 斯洛文尼亚"}, past the chalk cliffs of [Hampshire]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Hampshire · n. 汉普郡"}, maybe even as far as [Milwaukee]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Milwaukee 密尔沃基"} or the granite face of [Rushmore]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="rushmore · n. 拉石茂山"}. Somewhere outside [Bethlehem]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Bethlehem · n. 伯利恒"} or [Suriname]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Suriname · n. 苏里南共和国"}, perhaps, we would find the [secluded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="secluded · adj. 隐退的，隐居的；隐蔽的; 隔绝"} courtyard that every traveler is quietly looking for, the one that does not appear in any [Lexington]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Lexington 列克星敦"} guidebook but reveals itself only to the [stranded]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stranded · adj. 搁浅的；陷于困境的；有…股的; 搁浅"} and the unhurried.

### A Journey Without a Fixed Map

The old harbor town had long [territory]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="territory · n. 领土, 版图; 管区, 营业地区; 地盘, 领域, 范围"} no official chart had ever captured — its alleys were frankly [uncharted]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="uncharted · adj. 未知的;图上未标明的"}, and the [stairwell]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="stairwell · n. 楼梯井"} of the fifteenth-century watchtower still bore the faint geometric reliefs that any [Babylonian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Babylonian · n. 巴比伦居民；巴比伦城；巴比伦王国; 巴比伦的，与巴比伦有关的"} mason would have recognized as kin to the ziggurats of the Euphrates plain. Further east, the [expedition]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="expedition · n. 远征；探险；考察; 迅速，动作敏捷"} pushed into [subarctic]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="subarctic · adj. 亚北极区的"} highlands where the air tasted of iron and snow. The [castellated]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="castellated · adj. 造成城形的,构造如城的,有城的"} walls they finally found stood at a remarkable [elevation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="elevation."}, commanding a view of the entire [archipelago]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="archipelago · n. 群岛,列岛; 多岛屿的海"} that spread below like shards of green glass in grey water. A [provincial]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="provincial · adj. 大行政区的;省的; 褊狭的;守旧的;迂腐的; 首都以外的人;地区居民; 外省地;地方地"} museum back in the capital had once catalogued the site, but the records were lost during a period of mass [emigration]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="emigration · n. 移居外国；迁移出境; 移民"}: whole families forced to [repatriate]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="repatriate · vt. 把遣送回国, 遣返"} to coastal cities, leaving the highlands emptied.

In the lowlands, the contrasts grew sharper. [Mogadishu]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Mogadishu 摩加迪沙"}'s rebuilt seafront, [Singapore]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Singapore · n. 新加坡"}'s layered transit halls, the worn boulevard of [Louisville]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Louisville · n. 路易斯维尔"} beside the Ohio, the campus sprawl of [Chapel Hill]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Chapel Hill 教堂山"}, a cattle [squattage]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="squattage · n. 〈澳〉牧羊场主占有的财产"} outside a [Tennessee]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Tennessee · n. 田纳西州"} valley town, the oil-stained suburbs of [Venezuela]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Venezuela · n. 委内瑞拉"} — each place carried its own logic of [occupancy]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="occupancy · n. 占有, 使用, 居住; 占有期, 占用期"}, its own answer to the question of who belonged and who was merely passing through. In a sleek [Bangladesh]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Bangladesh · n. 孟加拉国"} guesthouse, the kitchen's [backsplash]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="backsplash 后挡板,后防溅板"} was tiled with a mosaic of the [Tyrrhenian]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Tyrrhenian · adj. 伊特鲁里亚的,伊特鲁里亚人的; 伊特鲁里亚人"} coastline — someone's homesick tribute to a sea they would never reach again. On the top floor a faded poster advertised charter flights to [Kyrgyzstan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Kyrgyzstan 吉尔吉斯斯坦，亚洲南部的一个国家，前苏联的一部分"}, destination of the latest wave of [venezuelan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="venezuelan · n. 白珍珠 Venezuelann. 委内瑞拉人; 委内瑞拉的,委内瑞拉人的"} expats chasing work across a world whose borders the old maps of [Singapore]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Singapore · n. 新加坡"}'s colonial era had never imagined.

### Layovers, Lobbies, and Lost Luggage

The old train car had been divided into a single [compartment]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="compartment · n. 间隔, 隔间"} for families, its [window-pane]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="window-pane · n. 窗玻璃"} fogged with the breath of restless children. A printed map on the wall traced the route [in all directions]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="in all directions 四面八方；向各方面；全面地"} — east toward the coast, west into the plains — with [demarcation]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="demarcation · n. 划界,立界; 分工"} lines showing which regions fell under separate rail authorities. It felt, somehow, like standing at the edge of [Mesopotamia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Mesopotamia · n. 美索不达米亚"}: ancient, unhurried, and very far from home.

After a connecting flight via the [Philippines]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Philippines · n. 菲律宾"}, the terminal at [Tallahassee]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Tallahassee · n. 塔拉哈西"} looked almost sleepy by comparison. The [baggage claim]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="baggage claim 行李认领；领取行李；取行李处"} carousel turned in slow circles, depositing suitcases onto the belt with a mechanical patience that matched the afternoon heat outside. A fellow traveler, returning to a [condominium]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="condominium · n. 共管的国家; 公寓"} near the water, said she had done this same loop — [Massachusetts]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Massachusetts · n. 马萨诸塞州"} to Florida and back — every winter for a decade. She had also lived briefly in [Connecticut]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Connecticut · n. 康涅狄格州"} and, before that, a rental in [Pennsylvania]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Pennsylvania · n. 宾夕法尼亚州"} that she remembered mainly for its drafty halls and a beautiful [mantelpiece]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="mantelpiece · n. 壁炉台"} above a fireplace nobody ever lit.

The lobby of the heritage hotel carried traces of older architectures: the clay plaster typical of [Mesoamerica]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Mesoamerica 中亚美利加洲,中美洲"}, the carved wooden headers you find across [Saskatchewan]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Saskatchewan · n. 萨斯喀彻温省"}, even a small brass plaque noting that the original owners had held diplomatic ties with [Saudi Arabia]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Saudi Arabia · n. 沙特阿拉伯"}. In one corner, a framed print showed [Montgomeryshire]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="Montgomeryshire 蒙哥马利郡"} in autumn, its hills impossibly green. Nobody seemed to know why it was there. Nobody asked. Travelers rarely do — they arrive, they look, they leave, scattering [in all directions]{.vocab tabindex="0" data-def="in all directions 四面八方；向各方面；全面地"} again before the place has a chance to explain itself.
